reasoning: History of loss of consciousness after head trauma in a young child is a high-risk mechanism for traumatic brain injury.
Head injury with LOC plus suspected arm fracture will require multiple resources (CT imaging, labs, orthopedic splinting/reduction, possible sedation).

HR 162 is elevated even for a 4-year-old (normal ~80-130) and RR 38 is at upper limits, raising concern for pain, stress, or early compensation for occult injury (e.g., intracranial or intra-abdominal).
Pediatric patients with head trauma and altered consciousness (even transient) should not wait; high-risk mechanism and possible evolving intracranial injury warrant ESI 2 despite current alertness.
Per ESI guidance, when torn between levels, choose the more acute option given risk of deterioration in pediatric head injury.
red_flags: Loss of consciousness after fall from height
Tachycardia and tachypnea out of proportion to visible injury
Pediatric head trauma with possible fracture
